claims.text: Linux load average includes runnable tasks and tasks in uninterruptible sleep, so a high load value is not equivalent to high CPU utilization and must be interpreted with CPU, blocked-task and wait evidence.

Linux PSI exposes CPU, memory and I/O pressure under /proc/pressure and measures time impact from resource contention, making it suitable for distinguishing resource-pressure stalls from simple capacity snapshots.
cgroup v2 provides scoped memory usage, event and pressure interfaces such as memory.current, memory.events and memory.pressure, so container diagnosis must not rely only on host-wide memory totals.

The first iostat report normally covers time since system startup while later reports cover the interval since the preceding report, and -y can omit the first report; interpreting an incident therefore requires the sampling window to be explicit.

sysstat documents %util near 100% as a saturation indication for devices that serve requests serially but warns that the metric does not express the performance limit of parallel devices such as RAID arrays and modern SSDs.
sar can collect, save and later report system activity records, enabling retrospective incident-window analysis when collection and retention were configured before the incident.
strace traces system calls and signals and is suitable for narrowed process-level diagnosis after the suspect process has been identified, rather than as a default global first probe.

Linux performance-monitoring facilities can expose sensitive execution data, supporting an explicit access, scope and production-safety boundary for deep performance probes such as perf; trace output can likewise contain process arguments and data that require controlled handling.
